sheet-71.description: The central and southern residential part of Leonia, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that Central Avenue (now Fort Lee Road) runs across the top. Grand Avenue curves down the left side and Broad Avenue runs down the right; between them lie blocks 299 to 312, crossed by Palisades Avenue, Prospect, the looping Crescent Avenue, Hill, Maple, Christie, Park Avenue and Highwood Avenue, with Romaine Place, Leonia Avenue, Gladwin Avenue, Oak Tree Place and Orchard Place as short cross streets. The blocks are thinly built with detached frame dwellings, a few with garages, sheds and summer houses; brick-veneered houses and a warehouse are scattered among them. Institutions are the Leonia Public School (steam heat, electric light) on Crescent Avenue east of Broad and the Leonia Episcopal Church on Park Avenue at Orchard Place. East of Broad Avenue the sheet shows the numbered lots of the Leonia Heights Land Co. tract (blocks 1 to 8) along Highland, Crescent, Allaire, Westview, Summit, Park, Highwood and Sylvan Avenues, with only a handful of houses. The lower third is the Leonia Terrace subdivision: long rows of narrow numbered lots (blocks 1 to 5) between Highwood and Sylvan Avenues, almost all vacant, with a short stretch of Sylvan Avenue beyond Broad at the lower right. Water pipes of 4 to 6 inches are drawn along most streets, with hydrants, and an acoustic alarm stands at Park and Broad Avenues. The scale bar and a north arrow appear on the sheet.
notes: Central Avenue is now Fort Lee Road; Palisades Avenue is now Palisade Avenue; Hill (between Crescent and Broad Avenues) is now High Street.
Highland is drawn as an unbuilt street between Leonia Heights blocks 1 and 2 north of Crescent Avenue; it was not used as control.
The lettering 'Leonia Heights Land Co.' runs up the lots east of Broad Avenue and 'Leonia Terrace' across the small lots between Highwood and Sylvan Avenues.

Leonia, central and south (Palisades volume, 1911, printed sheet 71): Central Av (now Fort Lee Road) at top to Sylvan Av at bottom, Grand Av on the left to Broad Av and the Leonia Heights lots on the right; Romaine Pl, Palisades Av (Palisade Avenue), Leonia Av, Gladwin Av, Oak Tree Pl, Prospect, Crescent Av, Hill (now High Street), Maple, Christie, Orchard Pl, Park Av, Highwood Av, Allaire, Westview, Summit Avs; Leonia Public School, Leonia Episcopal Church. One part. Scale 100 ft.

sheet-72.description: The northern part of Leonia, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) runs along the top edge and Broad Avenue along the bottom. At the upper left, beside the tracks, are the Leonia depot, a freight depot, coal sheds and H. J. Ferdon's coal yard with its wagon shed. Central Avenue (now Fort Lee Road) runs down the left edge, with Willow, Spring Street, Romaine Place and Gladwin Avenue entering from the left. Grand Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet, passing under a trolley line carried on a steel trestle that runs north from it; Schor Avenue leads north from Grand Avenue to the railroad, with Vogel's clothing factory on its east side and a short piece of Willow east of it. South of Grand Avenue are large, thinly built blocks (313 to 323) on Leonia Avenue, Woodbridge Place, Wood's Lane, Hillside (Riley) Avenue, Coover Street, Kingsley Street and Harrison Avenue, mostly frame dwellings with stables and sheds. The Presbyterian church stands on Central Avenue and the Leonia M.E. church on Kingsley Street; near Broad Avenue are a trolley station, a moving picture garden, the Coover-Hitchcock real estate office and an acoustic alarm. Below Broad Avenue the edge of blocks 324 to 326 shows Ripley Avenue and Harold Avenue. Much of the upper right of the sheet (block 314) is open land. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along the streets.
notes: Central Avenue is now Fort Lee Road; Willow is now Willow Tree Road; Woodbridge Place is now Woodridge Place; Harrison Avenue is now Harrison Street.
Hillside Avenue is lettered with the alternative name Riley in brackets; south of Broad Avenue the same line is lettered Ripley Avenue.

The junctions along Leonia Avenue, Hillside Avenue and Coover Street disagreed with the modern streets by 5 to 12 m in a consistent direction and were left out of the control; the sheet may be drawn slightly out of true in that area.
A trolley line on a steel trestle crosses the sheet north of Grand Avenue; the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) runs along the top edge.
A date, 2/6/11, is lettered in the lower right corner.

Leonia, north (printed sheet 72): Northern RR of N.J. (Erie) and Leonia depot at top left, Central Av (Fort Lee Road) on the left, Grand Av, Willow (now Willow Tree Road), Schor Av, Leonia Av, Woodbridge Pl (now Woodridge Place), Woods Lane, Hillside (Riley) Av, Coover St, Kingsley St, Harrison Av, Broad Av at bottom, Ripley Av, Harold Av; trolley on steel trestle; Presbyterian and M.E. churches. One part. Scale 100 ft. Leonia Av, Coover St and Hillside Av junctions (except Broad) disagree with modern streets by 5-12 m and are left out of the control.

sheet-73.description: The western edge of Leonia along the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie), drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that the railroad runs from top to bottom down the left half. Central Avenue (now Fort Lee Road) crosses the top of the sheet, with the end of Willow Street to the north of it. The business centre of the borough lies on Central Avenue east of the tracks: a livery stable, a blacksmith, stores and the Borough Hall with the fire department, the home of Leonia Hose Co. No. 1 and Hook and Ladder Co. No. 2 (28 volunteers, a hose reel, a hose wagon and a hook and ladder truck). Spring Street runs down the right half of the sheet lined on its west side by a row of two-storey dwellings, several stuccoed. Between Spring Street and Grand Avenue, which runs along the right edge with Palisades Avenue beyond it, are blocks 333 to 335 with a few larger houses and the Christian Reformed Church (hot-air heat, electric light) with its wagon shed. Prospect and Maple cross Spring Street; Willow runs south from Maple to the bottom edge between blocks 329 to 332. West of the railroad, block 327 is almost empty apart from a dwelling and two outbuildings on Central Avenue. Water pipes of 4 to 24 inches are drawn in the streets. The sheet carries its own scale of feet and a north arrow.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch, twice the scale of sheets 71 and 72.
Central Avenue is now Fort Lee Road; Willow Street north of Central Avenue is now Willow Tree Road; Palisades Avenue is now Palisade Avenue.
The southern Willow between Maple and the lower edge corresponds roughly to modern Station Parkway, which no longer follows the old line; it was not used as control.
Borough Hall and fire department of Leonia Hose Co. No. 1 and Hook and Ladder Co. No. 2 on Central Avenue.

Leonia, west by the railroad (printed sheet 73): Northern RR of N.J. (Erie) running down the sheet, Central Av (Fort Lee Road) at top, Spring St, Prospect, Grand Av, Maple, Willow St (Willow Tree Road), Palisades Av at the right edge; borough hall and fire department, Christian Reformed Church. One part. Scale 50 ft (scale bar of feet).
